bluf: iProspect is dentsu's performance media brand, an enterprise media agency claiming 8,000+ specialists across 93 countries, selling paid search, paid social, programmatic, retail media and SEO with no lead line. The record shows it winning big (it led the pan European BMW Group media win in 2025-07) and shedding leadership (a North America CEO exit reported 2026-04), with a house that runs its own Google and LinkedIn ads. The one thing a rival should know: the Horus read is Exposed at -14.9, most exposed to KJ6, and 15 of 17 clients on record are names only, with six of the 17 already on other tracked agencies' books.
doing:
iProspect positions itself as a global media agency of brand builders with a performance mindset, joining culture, content, data and technology with deep channel specialists: in plain words, a holdco media buying network asking to be read as a brand agency. Its headline claim is scale, 8,000+ specialists across 93 countries and 126 offices serving more than 2,600 clients, and its about page adds RECMA 2024 highest growth media network and MediaPost 2023 Search/Performance Agency of the Year.

The mix is ten services, from performance marketing and digital strategy through SEO, PPC, programmatic, retail media, paid social, video and digital OOH to affiliate marketing, with no line scoring above 2. Five core lines score 2. Paid Search rests on a dedicated PPC page built on experimentation and the MediaPost award. Paid Social rests on a page with FAQs and a TikTok travel case. Programmatic & CTV rests on programmatic, video and digital OOH pages detailing SSP and DSP partnerships. Retail Media rests on a Philips Amazon sales case and an Under Armour Amazon Advertising case. SEO rests on a page citing in house SEO tools and reporting and a Printful search leads case. No proprietary product and no partner is listed.

Its AI posture is AI built into performance work (consumer insight, digital strategy, paid social), with the SEO team publishing Google AI Mode guidance; AI Search / GEO and AI Automation / Agents score 1 each.

Moves in date order: 2025, a Google Ads Impact Award for data innovation; 2025-07, leading dentsu's pan European BMW Group media win with the mandate starting in 2026; 2026-04, the reported exit of the North America CEO, whom trade press names as Liz Rutgersson. No pricing signal is recorded. Absent for a network of this size: no jobs on record, no proprietary platform, Content & Digital PR, Email & CRM, Local and Web & Product at 0, and no office city, only countries.
clients:
The record marks the client type as enterprise and lists nine verticals: FMCG, beverages and spirits, real estate, travel and hospitality, automotive, telecom, consumer electronics and retail, apparel and industrial technology. Offices are listed by country only: the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, Denmark, Spain and Latin America.

The needs read names 17 clients, 2 observed and 15 names only. Under Armour is coded to paid performance and commerce from a slug reading amazon advertising, and Budweiser to paid performance from the title Advertising Campaign. The rest name the client and not the work. BMW Group and Siemens rest on dentsu press releases; the Siemens slug reads long term global SEA partnership, a search signal the needs read leaves uncoded. A&W, Elgiganten, Sonos and Tele2 carry titles reading marketing strategy, Parkdean Resorts reads Pandemic Travel Campaign and 1664 Bière reads Mobo Awards. The Printful title names no channel, although the SEO evidence note cites a Printful search leads case. Mitchum, Dubai Properties, Hilton, Carter's, IKEA and Hendrick's stand on case page URLs with no captured title. For these 15 the need is inferred from the sold mix, not observed.

Six of the 17 also sit on other tracked agencies' books: BMW Group (embryo, columbia-road), Siemens (merkle, diva-e), Under Armour (merkle, code-and-theory), Parkdean Resorts (rise-at-seven), Budweiser (mindgruve) and Sonos (instrument).

The Horus read is most exposed to KJ6, the hollowing of the agency middle, at -0.81 and to KJ5 at -0.18. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that enterprise buyers such as BMW Group and Siemens press for output or outcome pricing on the buying hours next, and a roughly even chance that the Amazon work shown for Under Armour becomes the route into ads inside AI answers (KJ2), a move the record shows no test of.
house: The record marks 3 of 4 say and do lines practised. Paid Search is corroborated by its own Google ads, 7 in the Transparency Center and 7 in the last 30 days. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated by 24+ ads of its own. Publishing cadence is corroborated by 401 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 650 in 365 out of 966. Paid Social is contradicted, the one gap listed: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. It publishes no llms.txt, blocks no AI crawlers and has 1 AI URL; the tag stack is gtm alone on Next.js. Its Google Ads Transparency Center record shows 7 ads, all text, under DENTSU UK LIMITED, last shown 2026-09-27. Its LinkedIn record shows 23 company ads and 1 thought leader ad, a floor; one sample reads "iProspect UK has won four awards at the Outdoor Media Awards 2026". No Meta or TikTok check is recorded.
market:
The Horus read puts iProspect at a tailwind index of -14.9, band Exposed. It is best placed for KJ2 at net 0.175 on Paid Search and AI Search / GEO, and for KJ1 at 0.117; it is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) at -0.81, driven by Paid Search, Paid Social and SEO, and to KJ5 at -0.18 on Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV. The best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 40/100. It is partial on P1, P2 and P4; P6, P7 and P8 are absent; P5 unknown; P3 does not apply.

The Monsoon read is 49.9, band Breeze, migration 59.9 against displacement 39.9, observed via the large network term, with holdco inferred and the enterprise ICP pulling down. 45 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (12) and Paid Search (8) most movable; the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, and automation overlaps 29%. No hub office is listed; it claims onshore delivery (in house SEO tools and reporting).
openings:
The strongest opening is the shopping book. Six of 17 clients sit on other tracked agencies' books and 15 of 17 are names without described work, so it is very likely, with moderate confidence, that BMW Group and Siemens, each on two other books, are contestable by a rival bringing a described result and a price: no described work stands behind either press release. Under Armour, with an Amazon advertising slug, is harder ground. The falsifier is a captured BMW Group or Siemens case study describing method and outcome.

The contradiction to lead with is paid social, sold with no social ad pixel on its own site, so a rival with the pixel on its own house can table the say and do test. The judgment exposure is KJ6 at -0.81, with P5 unknown, so a transparent outcome priced offer against media buying hours is a conversation it cannot have in public.

The move gaps are P8, no ads inside AI assistants despite a paid search core, and P4 partial, so the inputs automation consumes are the pitch against it. Displacement at 39.9 says the book does not buy on price: the offer that undercuts it is proof, not rate.
watch: Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would land directly on its KJ6 exposure and on dentsu's own disclosures.
Indicator I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, next reading late October 2026: at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation on the paid social line it sells without a pixel on its own site.

Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM would tell whether its KJ2 tailwind, ads inside AI answers, becomes a product while P8 stays absent.

Follow up the dated moves: the North America CEO exit reported 2026-04 and the BMW Group mandate starting in 2026, since a successor announcement or a first BMW Group campaign would change the leadership and delivery read.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
